description: A three-dimensional echo chamber shaped like a real crystal: rays are traced through the solid and four listeners inside it hear the reflections from four different places

params.text: Sets how big the crystal is, 0.06 to 24 metres; in Delay mode it sets the delay time instead
Sets how much of a ray is absorbed at each bounce, 1 to 60 per cent
Picks which of sixteen crystal habits the chamber is, ordered from a six-faced cube through to intergrown clusters
Sets how much reverberant tail is heard behind the discrete echoes
Sets the balance between the untreated signal and the chamber
Strikes the crystal with an internal striker on each press, entering at one emitter and then the other when the menu says so
Sets how long the internal striker rings, 0.05 to 4 seconds
Sets how many reflections are kept: few gives discrete rhythmic echoes and many gives a dense wash
Sets how much of what comes back re-enters the emitter, up to 92 per cent
Switches between Chamber, where arrivals land at the times the geometry really gives, and Delay, where the same arrival ratios are stretched out to musical times with the size knob setting the delay
Spins the drawing about that axis; the view is camera-only and moving it does not change what is heard
Places the pair of emitters along that axis of the crystal; they are the two ends of one axis rather than two loose points, which keeps the stereo image coherent

inputs.text: The signal entering the chamber at the first emitter
Changes the size, ±5V added to the size knob
Changes the absorption, ±5V added to the damping knob
Picks the crystal habit, one volt per habit from simple to complex
Changes the amount of tail, ±5V added to the tail knob
A rise strikes the crystal with the internal striker
Sets the pitch of the internal striker as a volt per octave
Changes the feedback, ±5V added to the feedback knob
The signal entering the chamber at the second emitter, which is where the other side of a stereo pair goes
Changes the dry and wet balance, ±5V added to the mix knob
Changes how many reflections are kept, ±5V added to the echoes knob

outputs.text: One of the four listeners inside the crystal; the four carry genuinely different arrival times and levels rather than one signal copied

notes: the module makes no sound of its own until something is patched in or the ping button is pressed; with nothing patched and the mix fully wet it is a bare resonator played by pinging
the emitter positions, their headings and the navigation speed are set on the display by dragging, and cannot be reached by clicking for help
the four emitter velocity CV inputs are declared in the code but have no jack on the panel, so a moving emitter can only be steered by dragging
changing the shape retraces the rays on a worker thread, taking about fifty milliseconds, and the new set of taps is faded in rather than switched, so it does not click
menu: Repeat pitch — a submenu putting a real pitch shifter in the recirculating loop, so each repeat rises or falls
Re-roll repeat pitches — draws a fresh set of repeat pitches; it appears only while the last Repeat pitch choice is selected
Ping alternates A / B — sends each press of the ping button to the other emitter in turn rather than always the first
Solid faces (occlusion) — draws the crystal solid so that near faces hide far ones, instead of as a wireframe
Draw on the panel (no screen) — lets the crystal be drawn across the whole panel rather than inside a screen rectangle
